title: sales-enablement-enterprise-playbook-positioning-messaging-competitive-pricing-case-studies-security-faq-2026-03-05
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook is a consolidated sales enablement reference for enterprise prospects evaluating Redwood Inference. It includes: core positioning and messaging, competitive brief summaries, an executive pitch deck outline, pricing guidance and negotiation levers, short customer case studies, and a Security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. Use this document in discovery and technical evaluation meetings; reference the related pages for deep technical or pricing details.

1) Executive positioning and core messaging

Intro (elevator):
- Redwood Inference delivers predictable, production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so engineering teams can ship features with consistent latency, cost, and reliability.

Value props (one-liners for different stakeholders):
- CTO/Platform: "Unified inference runtime and controls to standardize latency and cost across environments with enterprise-grade SLAs."
- VP of Product/Engineering: "Ship LLM features faster with a single API, built-in model management, and observability for quality and cost."
- Security/IT: "Private deployment options, KMS integrations, and audit logging to meet compliance requirements."
- Finance/Procurement: "Clear unit economics via token- and embedding-based billing, with dedicated and reserved capacity options to reduce per-token cost."

Positioning statement (for website/lead decks):
- "Redwood Inference: a developer-first inference platform that makes high-performance, reliable LLM serving predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

Messaging pillars (useable in sales scripts):
- Production-first: SLO-backed latency, intelligent fallbacks, and rolling updates built for customer-facing apps.
- Cost control: Batching, KV caching, and quantization guidance that meaningfully reduce per-token spend.
- Flexible deployment: Seamless parity between hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) installs.
- Observability & guardrails: Token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and quality monitoring integrated into CI.

2) Competitive brief (summary grid for quick reference)

Competitor | Redwood strength | Typical buyer concern | How we respond
---|---:|---|---
Cloud AI platforms | Lower unit cost at scale; unified runtime across environments | Concern about long-term vendor lock-in | Emphasize model-agnostic APIs and private deployment options; migration playbook in the onboarding kit
Managed LLM APIs | Simplicity of hosted endpoints | They may have broader model catalogs or custom models | Highlight our curated catalog with verified performance profiles and model-variant fallbacks for reliability
Self-hosted runtimes | Maximum control, potentially lower marginal cost | Operational burden and slower time-to-market | Position Redwood as the hybrid: managed control plane + optionally private/on-prem runtime, with runbooks and day-2 ops support
Inference infra vendors | Fine-grained kernel/runtime tuning | Integration and developer experience gaps | Call out our developer SDKs, observability console, and turnkey quantization profiles for common workloads

Top competitive messages to use in sales calls:
- "We provide enterprise parity: same API whether you choose Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments."
- "We focus on predictable economics — not just raw performance — so product teams can forecast costs reliably."

3) Pitch deck outline (5-8 slide executive summary)

Slide 1: Company & problem
- Quick statement: increased adoption of LLMs shifts competitive advantage to serving.

Slide 2: Solution overview
- Redwood Inference: runtime + orchestration + deploy options. Key bullets and one diagram (runtime, control plane, client app).

Slide 3: Differentiators
- Production-first tooling, unified runtime, cost levers, and private deployments. One-liner each + customer logos.

Slide 4: Performance & cost benchmarks
- Representative latency P50/P95 numbers for 8k/32k contexts, and unit cost comparisons (hosted vs. dedicated). Call out methodology and links to benchmark appendix.

Slide 5: Security & compliance
- Private deployment options, KMS/HSM support, audit logging, SOC/ISO (if applicable) statements and next steps for compliance review.

Slide 6: Pricing and engagement models
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated (reserved commit with burst), Private (license + support). Include typical procurement timelines.

Slide 7: Customer outcomes / case studies
- Short bullets on business impact (latency reduction, cost savings, uptime improvements).

Slide 8: Next steps / Evaluation plan
- Proposed pilot (4-8 weeks), success criteria (SLOs, cost delta, quality thresholds), and contacts.

4) Pricing guidance & negotiation levers

Pricing models (summary):
- Hosted API: usage-based billing (tokens for generation and embeddings).
- Dedicated: monthly/annual reserved capacity with predictable throughput and lower per-token costs.
- Private: platform license + optional support tiers and consulting for air-gapped/on-prem installs.

Common pricing anchors to use in negotiation:
- Pilot discount: offer a capped usage credit (typically 3-8 weeks) and waived onboarding for early pilots.
- Committed discounts: provide stepped discounts for 12/24/36 month reserved capacity commitments. Typical ranges: 15-35% depending on commit size and term.
- Volume/overage protections: include soft limits and auto-notifications before overage billing; offer temporary burst credits during PoC.
- Professional services: offer a separately scoped integration and day-2 ops package (SOW) -- useful for Private deployments.

Sample pricing scenarios (talking points, not contract language):
- Mid-market SaaS (10M monthly tokens): Recommend Dedicated with 12-month commit; expect 20-25% cost reduction vs. hosted.
- Large enterprise (sustained inference, 100M+ monthly tokens): Private or Dedicated with custom capacity planning and quantization profile consulting; outline multi-region considerations.

Negotiation playbook (steps):
1. Start with a time-boxed pilot: define KPIs (latency targets, cost per 1k tokens, quality regression thresholds).
2. Provide a tailored benchmark run and cost projection using the customer’s sample workload.
3. Move to a committed offer with stepped discounts and SLOs; document migration/runbook and support SLAs.

5) Case studies (short, sales-friendly abstracts)

Case study A -- Fintech scale-up (anonymized)
- Problem: customer-facing assistant had 400-600ms median latency spikes under peak traffic and erratic per-token costs.
- Redwood approach: implemented Dedicated reserved pools, KV prefix caching for common prompts, and batching for analytical backfill.
- Outcome: P50 latency improved from 520ms to 120ms; predictable per-token costs decreased by ~28%; error budget breaches eliminated in month 1.

Case study B -- Regulated healthcare provider
- Problem: strict data residency and audit requirements prevented hosted deployments; in-house stack was costly to operate at scale.
- Redwood approach: private deployment (VPC with customer-managed KMS), audit logging integration, and 2-week runbook handover.
- Outcome: achieved compliance checklist sign-off, reduced operational overhead for the customer platform team, and shortened incident TTR from days to hours.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (short answers for sales + technical reviewers)

Q: Can Redwood run fully on-prem / air-gapped?
A: Yes. We provide a Private deployment package that supports air-gapped installs. The package includes an installable runtime, offline license activation, and a runbook for upgrades and security reviews.

Q: How does Redwood handle customer keys and secrets?
A: We support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed key stores for Private deployments. Hosted customers can bring keys or use Redwood-managed keys with strict RBAC and rotation policies.

Q: What audit logging and access controls are available?
A: Audit logs capture control plane events, model rollouts, and admin actions. RBAC is configurable with roles for operators, SRE, and business users. Logs can forward to customer SIEMs via syslog or secure log ingestion endpoints.

Q: How do you ensure model output privacy during inference?
A: For Private deployments, customer data never leaves the customer network unless explicitly configured. For Hosted and Dedicated, we provide data handling agreements and options to disable telemetry; we also support per-customer data isolation and strict retention policies.

Q: Do you have penetration test / third-party attestations?
A: We engage third-party security firms for periodic pen tests and provide summaries to enterprise customers under NDA. Customers requiring detailed reports undergo a security review and can request relevant artifacts through the security team.

Q: What compliance frameworks do you support?
A: We maintain controls and evidence to support common frameworks (SOC-type controls, customer-facing GDPR controls, ISO readiness). For regulated customers, we coordinate an evidence package and scope-specific gap remediation during procurement.

7) Sales collateral checklist and playbook usage

Collateral to attach to outreach and evaluation:
- Executive pitch deck (this document's deck).
- Technical appendix: runtime architecture, benchmark methodology, and quant profiles.
- Security one-pager and SOC/ISO readiness overview.
- Pricing sheet and sample SOW for Private deployments.
- Customer references and case-study one-pagers.

Recommended usage patterns for reps:
- Discovery call: use the messaging pillars to map buyer pains and surface the relevant differentiator.
- Technical review: provide the technical appendix and connect the prospect to SE or solutions engineer for a benchmark run.
- Procurement: hand off pricing sheet and security evidence; offer a pilot + draft SOW to accelerate contracting.
